correctness.rationale: PASS: On c0(C), t_n=2^{-(n+1)} and (Az)_n=sum_{k>=1} t_n^k z_k. Row norms t_n/(1-t_n) are summable; exact operator norm ||A||=1/3, and A∘conjugation is real-nuclear (nuclear bound <=4/3). For 0<tau<3 the real-linear map I+tau A∘conjugation is a Neumann-series isomorphism, with ball inclusions and Hausdorff bound tau/3. Given nonzero f_a(y)=sum a_n y_n, f_a(Rz)=sum(a_k z_k+tau b_k conj(z_k)), b_k=sum_n a_n t_n^k, absolutely convergent. If its modulus attained a maximum on B, eventual |z_k|<1 allows complex coordinate perturbations ±w; the parallelogram identity forces a_k=b_k=0 for all sufficiently large k. Thus a is finitely supported, and for the first nonzero index n0 the moment asymptotic b_k/t_{n0}^k→a_{n0}≠0, a contradiction. No extrapolation from finite tests; this is an infinite-dimensional proof. Real-convex, not necessarily balanced, is essential.
